newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SELLS ELECTRIC FITTING MAKER FOR $604,000.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SELLS ELECTRIC FITTING MAKER FOR $604,000.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Friday it has sold 76 percent of electric fitting maker Elprom Naiden Kirov for $604,000.
It named the buyer as Costra Developpement Ins, which it said was linked to Israel's Electro Netech company dealing in electrotechnical equipment. Agency officials declined to elaborate.
Under the sale contract the buyer is due to pay half the price in cash and the other half either in cash or in Bulgarian Brady bonds.
The buyer also pledged to settle some 154 million levs ($630,000) of the company's debts and to invest at least $490,000 in the next five years.
Twenty percent of the company's capital will be offered to its staff at preferential prices and the remaining four percent will be used to meet restitution claims by former owners.
Elprom Naiden Kirov produces electrical switches, switchboards, plugs, sockets and fork-joints.
Its turnover for 1995 totalled 275.1 billion levs ($4.1 million). Forty percent of its output was exported last year, the agency said.
The agency said Costra Developpement Ins. had a $16 million turnover in 1995, of which $9 million were export revenues. It exported its output to Germany, Spain, Austria and the U.S.
Bulgaria issued three types of Brady bonds worth $5.2 billion in 1994 under a $8.16 billion foreign debt restructuring deal.
Discount bonds and Front Loaded Interest Reduction Bonds can be used as means of payment in Bulgaria's privatisation. -- Sofia Newsroom, +359-2 981 8569
